top_choice_rationale: Anne Carson (P001) remains my first choice on the merits of the work, from public knowledge and not fresh reading or independent verification. Her voice is distinctive and recognisable across decades, and the formal invention is how the work thinks, not ornament. Autobiography of Red recasts a fragmentary Greek source as a modern verse novel about desire and selfhood. Nox builds an elegy as a book whose form is part of the mourning. Eros the Bittersweet, Short Talks, The Beauty of the Husband and Decreation belong to the same practice of making an inherited form carry present grief and desire. The credit is limited to original verse narrative, elegy and essay, with the classical versions as context, which answers the delimitation concern. Her writing in English lowers one translation uncertainty but is not merit. I rank Cărtărescu (P002) a close second: his single, statable project is a real counterweight on unity and scale, and I would move to him if close reading showed Carson's later books repeat early devices. Neither case has verified later-work evidence, and the weighting between unity of project and breadth of reinvention is not settled by argument. Both proposals are preferred to no award (P000), since both oeuvres show voice, depth and sustained quality. Opening ranks and the count of supporters are not treated as evidence of merit.
